Refuse truck urban weekday data could possibly be combined with weekend data to augment low data availability that remained for urban weekend refuse data even after aggregation across hours. School and other buses do not have robust data by any means, but may be an improvement over non-source-specific default distributions. 5.2 Distributions of Distance Traveled In this next analysis, we calculated distance information, or VMT. Starting from the 10-second to 2-minute segments calculated for each vehicle, we determined the distance traveled and time spent in each hour, day type, road type, vocation, and source type. The number of hours the vehicle was instrumented with a data logger within each hour and day type was also tracked and is denoted the “instrumented hours.” We aggregated VMT distributions for each vehicle individually and saved the information to the files MilesDriven_source_hour_(fdna/cecert/combined).csv for hourly VMT distributions of each vehicle, MilesDriven_source_road_(fdna/cecert/combined).csv for the distribution of VMT spent driving on different road types, and MilesDriven_source_day_(fdna/cecert/combined).csv for the distribution of VMT between weekdays and weekends. We also generated the equivalent three files with the vocation given in addition to its source type for each vehicle ID and labeled these files MilesDriven_vocation_hour.csv, etc. These second three files contain the same distribution by vehicle as the first three, but the metadata column now includes their vocation as well. Each of these various groupings will be detailed in the following subsections. These results are developed using similar resolution to the three MOVES input tables—RoadTypeDistribution, day VMT fraction, and HourVMT fraction—and comparisons to MOVES inputs will be made throughout these subsections. 5.2.1 VMT Distribution by Road Type To calculate each of the distributions of distance traveled by source type or vocation, we used the “normalized sum over sum” approach used in the speed distribution calculations, which uses the “instrumented hours” to weigh each vehicle’s activity according to its utilization rate.
